The '''1994–95 Bundesliga''' was the 32nd season of the [[Bundesliga]], Germany's premier football league. It began on 19 August 1994<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=322729 |title=Schedule Round 1 |publisher=DFB |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110608092646/https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=322729 |archive-date=8 June 2011 }}</ref> and ended on 17 June 1995.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=323091 |title=Archive 1994/1995 Round 34 |publisher=DFB |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110608092701/https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=323091 |archive-date=8 June 2011 }}</ref> [[FC Bayern Munich]] were the defending champions.

This was the final season in which two points were awarded for a win; going forward this changed to [[Three points for a win|three points]].

==Competition format==
Every team played two games against each other team, one at home and one away. Teams received two points for a win and one point for a draw. If two or more teams were tied on points, places were determined by [[goal difference]] and, if still tied, by goals scored. The team with the most points were crowned champions while the three teams with the fewest points were relegated to [[2. Bundesliga]].

==Team changes to 1993–94==
[[1. FC Nürnberg]], [[SG Wattenscheid 09]] and [[Lokomotive Leipzig|VfB Leipzig]] were relegated to the [[1994–95 2. Bundesliga|2. Bundesliga]] after finishing in the last three places. They were replaced by [[VfL Bochum]], [[KFC Uerdingen 05|Bayer 05 Uerdingen]] and [[TSV 1860 Munich]].
